Empirical Research Plan ― Generic “Sharp-Change-at-Cutoff’’ Settings

====================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------
• Method:  Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).

• Why RDD?  
  – The probability of treatment jumps discontinuously at a known value z₀ of an observed assignment variable zᵢ.  
  – We are interested in the average causal effect for units “locally” at z₀, allowing for heterogeneous gains and even endogenous take-up.  
  – A fuzzy RDD delivers a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) equal to the ratio of the outcome jump to the treatment-probability jump at z₀ (local Wald estimator).  
  – RDD makes the **weakest possible** assumptions among standard quasi-experimental tools: continuity of potential outcomes in z around z₀; no need to assume homogeneous effects or absence of self-selection beyond the cutoff neighborhood.

====================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------
• Treatment indicator xᵢ: 1 if the unit actually receives the program; 0 otherwise.  
• Control units: observations with zᵢ < z₀ that do **not** receive the treatment; “untreated potential compliers’’ just to the left of the cutoff.  
• Treated units in the first stage: observations with zᵢ ≥ z₀ that do (or do not) take up the program, generating the jump in Pr(x=1|z).  
• Timing: cross-sectional; no time index needed.  
• Running variable zᵢ: the assignment score (test score, enrollment, distance, etc.).  
• Cutoff z₀: known administrative threshold set by the rule.

====================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------
A1. Continuity of Potential Outcomes  
    E[y₀ᵢ | zᵢ] and E[y₁ᵢ | zᵢ] are continuous in z at z₀.  
    Plausibility: Near-threshold students/households usually look similar; the rule is arbitrary.

A2. No Precise Manipulation of the Running Variable  
    Individuals cannot sort exactly to one side of z₀; the density of z is continuous at z₀.  
    Plausibility: Test scores, GPA, enrollment counts, and geographic boundaries are hard to manipulate at the margin, though not impossible (check).

A3. First-Stage Discontinuity (Relevance)  
    ΔPr(x=1|z₀⁺) – ΔPr(x=1|z₀⁻) ≠ 0.  
    Plausibility: Built into institutional rule.

A4. Monotonicity (for LATE interpretation)  
    No “defiers’’ who would take treatment only if assigned control.  
    Plausibility: Reasonable if assignment rule only raises, never lowers, take-up probability.

A5. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA) locally.  
    One unit’s treatment does not affect another’s outcome within small z window.

====================================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-----------------------------------------
T1. Manipulation / Sorting around z₀  
    • Test: McCrary density test (rddensity).  
    • Remedy: If mild, trim or use donut bandwidth (drop ±δ around z₀); if severe, credibility lost.

T2. Other Policies or Covariates Jump at z₀  
    • Test for discontinuities in predetermined covariates; run placebo outcomes.  
    • If detected, include covariates interacted with treatment or narrow bandwidth further.

T3. Functional-Form / Bandwidth Choice  
    • Use data-driven, MSE-optimal bandwidth (Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik).  
    • Report robustness to half and double the optimal bandwidth, and to global polynomials of order 1–3.

====================================================================
5. R Code Outline
-----------------
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast data
library(rdrobust)        # RD estimation
library(rddensity)       # McCrary test
library(fixest)          # alternative OLS

# 1. Load Data --------------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("myRDDdata.csv")  # columns: id, y, x, z, cov1, cov2, ...

# 2. Basic Variable Construction -------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0                                 # set z0 (modify as needed)
dt[, running := z - cutoff]                 # center at cutoff
dt[, treat_rdd := (running >= 0)]           # assignment indicator

# 3. First-Stage Check ------------------------------------------------------
fs <- rdrobust(y = x, x = running, c = 0)
print(fs$Estimate)      # should be significantly ≠ 0

# 4. Main (Fuzzy) RD Estimate ----------------------------------------------
main <- rdrobust(y = y, x = running, fuzzy = x, c = 0,
                 kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
summary(main)           # LATE = τ̂

# 5. Covariate Balance ------------------------------------------------------
covs <- c("cov1", "cov2")
lapply(covs, function(v){
  bal <- rdrobust(y = dt[[v]], x = running, c = 0)
  print(bal$coef)
})

# 6. Density Test -----------------------------------------------------------
dens <- rddensity(X = running, c = 0)
summary(dens)

# 7. Robustness: Bandwidth Sensitivity --------------------------------------
for (bw in c(main$bws[1]/2, main$bws[1]*2)){
  rob <- rdrobust(y = y, x = running, fuzzy = x, h = bw, p = 1)
  cat("h =", bw, "  LATE =", rob$coef[1], "\n")
}

# 8. Optional Donut RD (drop ±0.5 units) ------------------------------------
dt_donut <- dt[abs(running) > 0.5]
donut <- rdrobust(y = dt_donut$y, x = dt_donut$running,
                  fuzzy = dt_donut$x, c = 0)
summary(donut)
```

====================================================================
6. Expected Results
-------------------
Because the method note is generic, no single sign or magnitude can be asserted. In a typical merit-scholarship setting we expect:
• Positive LATE on college attendance (≈ 5-10 p.p. increase).  
• Positive effect on educational attainment (≈ 0.2–0.4 years).  
But these are purely illustrative priors.

====================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = clearly satisfied; 0 = questionable)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No precise manipulation of z at z₀ ………………… 1  
C2. Continuity of potential outcomes in z ………… 1  
C3. First-stage discontinuity is sizeable …………… 1  
C4. No other simultaneous discontinuities …………. 0.5 (needs testing)  
C5. Sufficient data density near cutoff ……………… 1  

Overall: 4.5 / 5. The design is likely credible, subject to diagnostic tests above.

====================================================================
End of Plan
